title: The Decision, the sequel - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Tyler Cowen uses LeBron James's free-agency choice as a revealed-preference exercise: each plausible destination maps to a different terminal objective, and by signing with Philadelphia rather than Golden State, Miami, Los Angeles or Cleveland, LeBron revealed he was maximizing title odds with a team that had not just won one. Cowen turns it into a question for the reader about what their own final major career decision will optimize.

insights.claim: Cowen frames the close of a career as a forced ranking among distinct terminal objectives — earning an especially large sum of money, publishing a final wonderful paper, or performing an amazing act of mentorship.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A usable lens for reading late-career moves by CEOs, founders and fund managers: the destination chosen discloses the objective function they never state publicly.
insights.quote: Imagine your career were coming to a close, how would you want it to end?
insights.locator: Imagine your career were coming to a close

insights.claim: Cowen closes by turning the exercise back on the reader, asking what their own final major career decision will look like — treating the choice set as a diagnostic rather than a sports story.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: The transferable point: enumerate each option's implied objective before deciding, because the option you pick will be read as your true priority.
insights.quote: What will your final major career decision look like?
insights.locator: What will your final major career decision look like?

themes.theme: Mapping each destination to an objective

insights.claim: Had LeBron wanted to finish his career alongside the teammates he most enjoys playing with, the choice would have been Golden State with Steph and Draymond; had he wanted his favored organization, it would have been Miami.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Each foregone option is priced information — the ones passed over show which motives were dominated.
insights.locator: When it comes to Lebron, had he wanted to finish

insights.claim: Staying in Los Angeles would have meant furthering son Bronny's NBA prospects and getting more family time, while Cleveland would have been the hometown sentimental choice.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Family and legacy motives were on the table and were rejected — a data point against the assumption that dynastic or hometown considerations dominate at end of career.
insights.locator: Furthering the NBA prospects of his son Bronny

insights.claim: LeBron James signed with Philadelphia, which Cowen reads as revealing that he wanted to maximize his chances of winning a title — and specifically with a team that had not just won one, ruling out OKC and NYC.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Where marquee talent goes late in a career signals which franchises are perceived as under-monetized contenders, which feeds franchise valuation and media-rights narratives.
insights.quote: As it turned out, he wanted to maximize his chances of winning a title, and with a team that did not just win a title
insights.locator: As it turned out, he wanted to maximize his chances
